title: Find the Town Judge
summary: People are numbered from 1 through n.

contractDetails.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000. 0–10000 distinct directed trust pairs with endpoints in [1,n] and no self-trust.
contractDetails.output-checking: Directed trust edges have one-based labels. Compare the exact judge label or −1.

statement: People are numbered from 1 through n. A row [a,b] means a trusts b. Find the person trusted by every other person who trusts nobody. Return that label, or −1 if no such person exists.

examples.explanation: Everyone else trusts 4, and 4 trusts nobody.
The only person meets both conditions vacuously.

constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000. 0–10000 distinct directed trust pairs with endpoints in [1,n] and no self-trust.
hints: Conceptual: Trust toward and away from a person count differently.
Directional: Keep counts of incoming and outgoing trust.
Implementation: Look for someone with n−1 incoming pairs and zero outgoing pairs. With unique pairs, one signed difference per person is enough.
complexityAnalysis: O(n+t) time and O(n) auxiliary space, where t is the pair count.
